def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Locate the repeated horizontal color strip.
    strip_rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v != 0 for v in grid[r]) >= 2]
    # The shape is the nonzero component not belonging to the strip.
    from collections import deque
    cells = {(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != 0}
    comps = []
    while cells:
        start = cells.pop()
        comp = {start}
        q = [start]
        while q:
            r, c = q.pop()
            for p in ((r-1,c),(r+1,c),(r,c-1),(r,c+1)):
                if p in cells:
                    cells.remove(p)
                    comp.add(p)
                    q.append(p)
        comps.append(comp)

    # Repeated strip has the same colored cells in several rows.
    strip = max(comps, key=len) if len(comps) > 1 else set()
    # Identify strip cells by columns with identical nonzero values in consecutive rows.
    color_cols = []
    for c in range(w):
        vals = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if grid[r][c] != 0]
        if len(vals) >= 2 and len(set(vals)) == 1:
            color_cols.append((c, vals[0]))
    colors = [v for _, v in color_cols]

    shape_comp = min(comps, key=len)
    # In case the strip was split into components, select the component whose
    # bounding box is the small irregular silhouette.
    sr = [r for r, c in shape_comp]
    sc = [c for r, c in shape_comp]
    r0, c0 = min(sr), min(sc)
    shape = {(r-r0, c-c0) for r, c in shape_comp}
    sh = max(r for r, c in shape) + 1

    # Align the stack so the copy matching the original color remains in place.
    original_color = grid[r0][c0]
    if original_color not in colors:
        original_color = grid[r0][next(c for c in range(w) if grid[r0][c] != 0)]
    idx = colors.index(original_color)
    top = r0 - idx * sh
    out = [[0] * w for _ in range(h)]
    for i, color in enumerate(colors):
        for dr, dc in shape:
            r, c = top + i * sh + dr, c0 + dc
            if 0 <= r < h and 0 <= c < w:
                out[r][c] = color
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Find the repeated palette strip: a row with a multi-color sequence
    # occurring identically on several rows.
    sequences = {}
    for r, row in enumerate(grid):
        cols = [c for c, v in enumerate(row) if v != 0]
        if len(cols) >= 2:
            seq = tuple(row[c] for c in cols)
            sequences.setdefault(seq, []).append(r)
    palette = max(sequences, key=lambda seq: len(sequences[seq]))
    rows = sequences[palette]

    # Exclude palette-strip cells, then collect the color-1 template.
    strip_rows = set(rows)
    shape_cells = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                   if grid[r][c] == 1 and r not in strip_rows]
    r0 = min(r for r, c in shape_cells)
    r1 = max(r for r, c in shape_cells)
    c0 = min(c for r, c in shape_cells)
    c1 = max(c for r, c in shape_cells)
    shape = {(r-r0, c-c0) for r, c in shape_cells}
    sh = r1 - r0 + 1

    # Tile the silhouette in palette order, preserving the position of its 1 copy.
    idx = palette.index(1)
    top = r0 - idx * sh
    out = [[0] * w for _ in range(h)]

            if 0 <= rr < h and 0 <= cc < w:

    return out
